title: Bounded execution of a counted loop
statement: Fix a program environment, resource limits, and execution depth, and let $i$ be a local variable, $h$ an expression, and $B$ a loop body. Let $X$ be a list of local indices, $I(j,\mu)$ an invariant on a counter value $j$ and memory $\mu$, and $Q$ a postcondition on states. Suppose $I(0,\mu)$ holds; for every $j<n$, every local store $\ell'$, and every memory $\mu'$ satisfying $I(j,\mu')$, executing $B$ from the state whose locals are the frame of the list obtained by refreshing $\ell'$ along $X$ and then setting local $i$ to $j$, with memory $\mu'$, can finish with cost at most $b$ and memory satisfying $I(j+1,\cdot)$. Suppose also that whenever $I(n,\mu')$ holds, $Q$ holds of that same framed state with local $i$ set to $n$; that for every $j\le n$ satisfying the invariant, $h$ is safe in that state and has value $n$; that every local assigned by $B$ belongs to $X$; that $i\notin X$; that $n\le\mathrm{word}$; and that $n(\mathrm{cost}(h)+b+7)+\mathrm{cost}(h)+5\le T$. Then the counted loop starting from the state with locals given by the frame of $\ell$ and memory $\mu$ can finish with cost at most $T$ in a state satisfying $Q$.
hypotheses_covered: Each iteration for $j<n$ preserves the invariant and has cost at most $b$ from the specified refreshed frame with counter $j$
At $j=n$, the specified framed state satisfies $Q$ whenever the invariant holds
For every $j\le n$ satisfying the invariant, the loop bound expression is safe and evaluates to $n$ in the specified state
Every local assigned by the body belongs to $X$
The counter index $i$ is not in $X$
